question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle Given Its Velocity
question.problem: A particle moves with a constant velocity of $u=(2i-5j)\,\text{m/s}.$ Find the speed of the particle, rounding your answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The speed of a particle equals the magnitude of its velocity.

Therefore, the speed of the particle is

$$
\begin{aligned}|u| & =|2i-5j| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-5)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+25} \\  & =\sqrt{29} \\  & ≈5.39\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle Given Its Velocity
question.problem: A particle moves with a constant velocity of $u=(i+4j)\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the speed of the particle, rounding your answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The speed of a particle equals the magnitude of its velocity.

Therefore, the speed of the particle is

$$
\begin{aligned}|u| & =|i+4j| \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+16} \\  & =\sqrt{17} \\  & ≈4.12\,\text{km/h}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Final Velocity of a Particle
question.problem: The velocity of a particle is $(-i+4j)\,\text{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\text{h}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2i+j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=6\,\text{h}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=-i+4j,\,a=2i+j.
$$

Therefore, after $t=6\,\text{h},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(-i+4j)+(2i+j)(6) \\  & =(-i+4j)+(12i+6j) \\  & =(11i+10j)\,\text{km/h}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle
question.problem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(-2i-8j)\,\text{m/s},$ and when $t=4\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $2i\,\text{m/s}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=-2i-8j,\,v=2i,\,t=4,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 2i & =(-2i-8j)+a(4) \\ 4i+8j & =4a \\ a & =\frac{1}{4}(4i+8j) \\  & =(i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Time when a Particle Reaches a Particular Velocity
question.problem: A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(3i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$ The velocity of the particle is $(-7i-6j)\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $2i\,\text{m/s}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
a=3i+2j,\,u=-7i-6j,\,v=2i
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 2i & =(-7i-6j)+(3i+2j)t \\ 9i+6j & =(3i+2j)t \\ 9i+6j & =3ti+2tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $i$ and $j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}9=3t \\ 6=2t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,t=3\,\text{s}.
$$
